decor.hgdwText: A brass plate at the foot of the statues: The Four Saints of the Garden. Knight, smith, lady, child. They stood on the lawn for three hundred years and the pond has had them for ten.
decor.hgt: A brass plate at the foot of...
decor.label: Four Saints

decor.hgdwText: The archivist moved the abbey library down here when the pond began to rise. She said books should be kept where they cannot burn. She did not say what else the water would keep.
decor.label: The Archivist

decor.hgdwText: Cut into the rim of the bell: I RANG ONCE WHEN THE WATER CAME IN. THE WHOLE VALLEY HEARD ME. NOBODY CAME. I WILL NOT RING AGAIN.
decor.label: The Bell

decor.hgdwText: Scratched on the boat: The ferry made the crossing every dawn for forty years. The last passenger paid with a button. The ferryman kept it, and the boat, and the pond kept him.
decor.label: The Ferry

decor.hgdwText: A shrine to the pond saint, who is said to have walked across the water. The water rose, and the saint stayed exactly where she was. The candle in the niche has not gone out.
decor.label: Pond Saint

decor.hgdwText: Written on the frame: It shows this same passage, but dry, with the lamps lit, and a door at the end that is not here. Do not look for long.
decor.label: Mirror Frame

decor.hgdwText: A diver's slate: Hest went in for the pearls with one helm between two of us. I held the rope. The rope held. I do not know about the rest. The chest by my knee is his share.
decor.label: Diver's Slate

decor.hgdwText: Scratched on a clam shell: Pearls grow slowly here, one for each year a stranger stays away. This grotto is very rich.
decor.label: Clam Shell

decor.hgdwText: A small brass plate: Fair measure. Every pearl taken from the deep is weighed here, and the deep takes its tenth. Take what is yours and leave the tenth on the pan.
decor.label: Fair Measure

decor.hgdwText: Chalked on a crate: CARGO FOR THE ABBEY. DO NOT OPEN BEFORE LENT. The crates were opened long ago, by the water, and there was only lamp oil inside. It is all still here.
decor.label: Cargo Notice

decor.hgdwText: A fisher's note: I hung three lanterns here so that nobody would be lost in the dark. If you can see this one, you are not lost yet. Follow the glow back to the wide room.
decor.hgt: A fisher's note: I hung three...
decor.label: Fisher's Note

decor.hgdwText: The stone says, in square letters: THE DEEP WEIGHS ALL THINGS. IT HAS NOT YET FOUND ANYTHING LIGHTER THAN A KINDNESS.
decor.label: The Rune

decor.hgdwText: Scratched small: A dead end. I came all this way for a dead end.
decor.label: Scratched Words

decor.hgdwText: Chalked: Turn back. The reeds are thicker beyond, and there is no beyond.
decor.label: Chalk Marks

decor.hgdwText: Written in oil: Two lefts, one right, and you are here. Two rights, one left, and you are not.
decor.hgt: Two lefts, one right, and you...
decor.label: Oil Writing

decor.hgdwText: Scratched: Somebody sat here a long time. The weed on the floor is flattened in the shape of a person.
decor.hgt: Somebody sat here a long time
decor.label: Scratched Words

decor.hgdwText: Carved: I counted forty breaths of air on this side of the maze. Spend them on the middle, not on the corners.
decor.hgt: I counted forty breaths of air...
decor.label: Old Inscription

decor.hgdwText: A fisher's mark, three lines and a hook: Good eels in the weed here. Bad eels in the weed next door.
decor.label: Fisher's Note

decor.hgdwText: Chalked: My brother says the walls are the same green as the water. They are not. The water is greener.
decor.hgt: My brother says the walls are...
decor.label: Chalk Marks

decor.hgdwText: NOTICE. Beyond this board the water belongs to the Warden of the Deep. Divers who wish to keep their helms should turn back, and divers who do not should at least take someone with them.
decor.label: Warden's Notice

decor.hgdwText: Carved in the wall at the crossing: THE STEPS UP, 22 squares on, by the east passage. THE WARDEN, 42 squares on, by the north passage. The water does not care which you choose.
decor.label: Signpost

decor.hgdwText: A lantern-maker's mark and two lines of chalk: Up and out is 46 squares, west first. The Warden sleeps 24 squares off, north first. Someone has scratched out a third line here, and then written it again.
decor.label: Signpost

decor.hgdwText: Painted on the stone in fading white: Dry land, 56 squares away, start north. The big room with the Warden in it, 68 squares away, start west. Trust the arrows. Do not trust the weed.
decor.label: Signpost

decor.hgdwText: Scratched with a spoon handle: If you are tired, the steps up are 86 squares, north. If you are brave, the Warden is 60 squares, north. Count your breaths at every crossing.
decor.label: Waymarker

decor.hgdwText: A ferryman's tally, cut deep: Air above, 42, leave south. Trouble below, 30, leave north. The numbers are squares. The fish keep to the left. Do as they do.
decor.label: Signpost

decor.hgdwText: Chiselled in neat capitals: STAIRS 46 (WEST). WARDEN 30 (EAST). KEEP TO THE MIDDLE OF THE PASSAGE. Do not stop here. Do not stop anywhere that has a sign.
decor.label: Signpost

decor.hgdwText: Written in lamp oil on a wet beam: I counted it twice. 97 squares to the stairs, going east. 52 squares to the Warden, going east. The ink is the pond's. It will not last, so read it now.
decor.label: Waymarker

decor.hgdwText: A sailor's rhyme, scratched small: 59 to the light, 14 to the dark. The light lies south from here, the dark lies south. Someone has underlined the word nearest, twice.
decor.label: Signpost

decor.hgdwText: Scratched under the bell frame: Cast in the abbey foundry, blessed by seven monks. The water has blessed it since, and the bell has been very quiet about its feelings.
decor.label: Bell Frame

decor.hgdwText: A ticket stub stuck to the hull: One crossing, any dawn. Paid in full. Not refundable, not returnable, not afloat.
decor.hgt: A ticket stub stuck to the hull:...
decor.label: Ferry Ticket

decor.hgdwText: Small offerings crowd the niche: a button, a pearl, a child's tooth. The saint has refused none of them.
decor.label: Offerings

decor.hgdwText: A second card tucked into the frame: Whoever stands in front of this glass sees the lamps lit and the door open. Whoever stands beside it sees only water. Stand beside it.
decor.label: Mirror Card

decor.hgdwText: Scratched on a tin cup: Hest, if you come back for your share, the lantern is still lit. I did not wait long. I waited as long as the oil lasted.
decor.hgt: Hest, if you come back for your...
decor.label: Diver's Cup

decor.hgdwText: Chalked on the rock: Count the pearls twice. The clams count them too, and they have never once lost count.
decor.label: Clam Warning

decor.hgdwText: Weights stacked beside the scales, each stamped with a name. The smallest says Kindness. The largest says Gold. They weigh exactly the same.
decor.label: Stamped Weights

decor.hgdwText: A ledger page weighed down with a keg: Forty crates in, thirty nine out. The fortieth is under here somewhere. Do not ask what is in it.
decor.hgt: A ledger page weighed down with...
decor.label: Cargo Ledger

decor.hgdwText: A fisherman's knot tied round the lamp hook: For luck, and for finding the way back.
decor.label: Fisher's Note

decor.hgdwText: Small stones piled at the foot of the tall slab, one for each visitor who read the letters aloud. There are only three. The rest read them quietly.
decor.hgt: Small stones piled at the foot...
decor.label: Pilgrim Stones

decor.hgdwText: Pinned under the notice: the names of divers who read this and went on. The list is long and the ink is fresh.
decor.label: Diver Names
